idiom_name: one class per surface over the driver/toolkit API, with GoogleTest fixtures owning the session
implementation_notes: C++ classes implement the classic structure directly: each page is a class holding the driver handle and typed accessors, and its methods return primitives or the next page object. What is missing is a page-object library - GoogleTest supplies the runner, fixtures (SetUp/TearDown) and assertions, but nothing initialises element fields - so the page base class, the element lookup and the wait policy are hand-written; Qt Test or a commercial GUI-test tool integrates at the toolkit level instead. Keep the driver handle private, let the fixture own session lifetime, and re-query per action rather than caching raw elements.
pitfalls: Element proxies or raw element handles stored in a member can dangle after navigation; re-query inside each method unless the element is provably stable.
The driver is not thread-safe and GoogleTest may run tests in parallel: give each test its own session via the fixture instead of sharing a page object behind a static driver.

Navigation methods that return page objects by value require every page class to include its successors - or to return a variant or enum target the test resolves; mixing both policies produces include cycles.
